Anomalous behavior will be flagged after which servicing and maintenance can occur. 3.3 Year 3: Advanced “Smart Facility” In Year 3, the team will be focused on the following high-level tasks: • Power and energy consumption optimization • Resilience and cybersecurity maximization 3.3.1 Power and Energy Consumption Optimization NREL acquires its power and energy consumption data using a variety of systems. Key amongst these systems are: • Data acquisition from facility power meters (typically GE) through a Delta system (480VAC, typically 400A and 800A feeds) • VFD power measured by the various pump/fan VFDs • ModbusTCP data acquisition from Emon/Dmon, Satec, and Schneider smart breakers (480VAC/277VAC, 3-phase circuits, 20A to 150A) • Schneider/APC power distribution (415VAC/240VAC, 3-phase circuits 20A or 40A) • Power measured at rack PDUs (most) • In some cases, power measured at the sub-rack level (e.g., via Ursa Major for Peregrine) and node-level for the HPC platforms. • This task will focus on investigating power and energy consumption optimization. To start, NREL and HPE will focus on one or more of the following areas: • Energy-aware job scheduling A. Apply machine learning approaches to predict the application/job power/energy footprint. B. Optimizing the SLURM resource manager, it has the application profile information from the data analytics tool so it can schedule the job at the appropriate time. • Managing power consumption to minimize utility demand charges • Dialing back power usage when time-of-use rates are high 4 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. 3.3.2 Resilience and Cybersecurity Maximization This task will focus on resilience and cybersecurity within the following areas: • Taking actions in response to a changing energy profile for a known user. The changing energy profile may suggest an unauthorized user. • Providing ongoing oversight and authentication for registered users • Numerous additional opportunities to improve resilience and cybersecurity exist, and additional focus areas may be added as time permits. Modification 1 Task 3.2.1: Kraken Mare (KM) Implementation – Partial A partial demonstration of the Kraken Mare (KM) data infrastructure will be performed using the Cooling Rack metrics. NREL deliverables: • Provide platform to support KM components for AIOps workloads, ensuring re-use of any existing hardware/software/data already installed at NREL or on Eagle. • Provide schema to be used with Avro for time-series metrics in collaboration with HPE. • Ensure that Cooling Rack Controller (CRC) metrics are streaming and available on Kafka. HPE deliverables: • Provide a design concept for implementation/integration of KM modules and the integration requirements in the data center. • Provide script that reads metrics from CRC and provides them in Avro serialized format to Kafka. • Create spreadsheet of sensor registration values for use in Task 2. Task 3.2.2: Kraken Mare Implementation – “Full” A more complete demonstration of the Kraken Mare (KM) data infrastructure will be performed using a more complete list of metrics agreed upon by NREL and HPE.
